result.instructions: Call get_guide first, then profile_show for the team's robot.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Read this FIRST. Describes the server, its epistemic guardrails, and the intended workflow (load a robot profile, then analyze).

tools.name: log_info
tools.description: Summary of a .wpilog: version, entry count, duration.

tools.name: log_entries
tools.description: List entries (signals) in a .wpilog, optionally filtered by a name substring.

tools.name: read_entry
tools.description: Read decoded samples for one entry (capped).

tools.name: ingest_log
tools.description: Parse a .wpilog and persist its summary + entry index into a SQLite trend store (so season queries don't re-parse).

tools.name: power_analysis
tools.description: Brownout/battery analysis over a log's voltage signal. Hedged, quality-scored. (The 2026 energy-management meta.)

tools.name: can_health
tools.description: CAN error-count analysis over a log. Hedged.

tools.name: profile_show
tools.description: Show a robot profile (YAML) so analysis is robot-specific (CAN map, drivetrain, subsystems).

tools.name: profile_init
tools.description: START HERE for a team that has not used this tool before. Scans a WPILib robot repository and generates the robot profile every other tool reads — CAN IDs, drivetrain geometry, PathPlanner settings, vendordeps — so analysis is specific to THIS robot instead of generic. Writes the profile only when 'out' is given; otherwise it is a dry run you can review first. Always surface the warnings it returns: CAN IDs the code marked TODO/NOT ACCURATE are guesses, and acting on a wrong CAN ID sends a human to check the wrong motor.

repo.description: Path to the team's WPILib robot repository (the directory with src/main/java and, usually, src/main/deploy/pathplanner)

out.description: Where to write the profile .yaml (omit for a dry run)

team.description: FRC team number, if not discoverable

tools.name: pathplanner_show
tools.description: Summarize a PathPlanner .path (waypoints, constraints).

tools.name: pathplanner_fudge
tools.description: Propose translating a waypoint by (dx,dy) meters. Returns a reviewable diff; writes only if 'out' is given.

tools.name: pathplanner_set_speed
tools.description: Propose new global max velocity/accel for a path. Reviewable diff; writes only if 'out' is given.

tools.name: pathplanner_move_marker
tools.description: Retime an event marker — the 'timing' half of a between-match autonomous tweak (e.g. spin the flywheels up earlier). Positions are waypoint-relative, NOT seconds: the integer part is a waypoint index and the fraction is progress along the next segment, so a path with N waypoints spans 0..N-1. Call pathplanner_show first to see the markers and their current positions. A ranged marker keeps its length when moved, unless you pass endPos. Reviewable diff; writes only if 'out' is given.

delta.description: Retime by this much, relative to the marker's current position (negative = earlier). Use instead of 'pos'.

endPos.description: New end position for a ranged marker; null converts it to a point marker. Omit to preserve the existing length.

tools.name: pathplanner_set_zone
tools.description: Move a constraint zone, or change a constraint inside it (e.g. maxVelocity, to slow the robot through one tight passage without slowing the whole path — which is what pathplanner_set_speed does). Bounds are waypoint-relative, not seconds. Reviewable diff; writes only if 'out' is given.

key.description: Constraint to change inside the zone, e.g. maxVelocity, maxAcceleration, maxAngularVelocity (with value)

tools.name: loop_check
tools.description: Verify a scenario's success criteria against a log (the closed-loop 'verify' step). Returns per-check PASS/FAIL.

tools.name: loop_suite
tools.description: Run a whole regression suite (a directory of scenarios) against a log — every banked fix re-checked at once.

tools.name: loop_iterate
tools.description: Run ONE full turn of the agentic closed loop: rebuild the robot code, run it headless, verify every scenario against the log it produced, and diagnose what failed. Use this after editing robot code — it reports build errors, missing logs, and misbehaviour as distinct outcomes, and says which checked values moved since your last edit. Requires a loop.yaml in the project.

config.description: Path to loop.yaml or a directory inside the project (default: cwd)

scenario.description: Check a single scenario .yaml instead of the whole suite

inputLog.description: For a REPLAY config (its run command uses {inputLog}): the recorded .wpilog to replay this turn, instead of the one the config names. This answers 'what would my change have done on THIS match' without resimulating. Ignored by sim configs.

tools.name: smallmodel_train
tools.description: Train a tiny logistic classifier from a few moments YOU mark in a log — the 'big AI trains a small AI' technique. The use case is a judgement call with no sensor for it (e.g. the right moment to stage game pieces): mark ~30 good moments, learn a predictor over chosen signals, save it as readable JSON that can be checked into the robot repo. Timestamps are SECONDS of log time. Metrics returned are TRAINING-set metrics — they show the model fit your marks, not that it generalizes; validate with smallmodel_score on a different log.

log.description: Path to the .wpilog to learn from

out.description: Where to write the model JSON

signals.description: Feature signal names, exactly as they appear in the log (use log_entries to find them)

positives.description: Timestamps (seconds) you are marking as the positive class

negatives.description: Explicit negative timestamps (seconds). Omit to draw negatives from the rest of the log.

stride.description: When drawing negatives, take every Nth sample (default 10)

threshold.description: Decision threshold (default 0.5; raise it to cut false positives)

tools.name: smallmodel_score
tools.description: Run a saved small model over a log and report where it fires, highest-scoring moments first. This is how you validate a model against a log it was not trained on before trusting it on the robot.

model.description: Path to a model JSON from smallmodel_train

top.description: How many top moments to list (default 10)

tools.name: loop_history
tools.description: The iteration journal for a project: every previous turn, which source files changed, and how each checked value moved. Read this when resuming work to see what has already been tried.

config.description: Path to loop.yaml or a directory inside the project (default: cwd)

tools.name: loop_generate
tools.description: Derive a regression scenario from a run that is known to be good, so a verified fix can be banked as a standing check. Proposes thresholds for counters, battery voltage, loop period, and converging errors. Dry-run unless 'out' is given. Review the thresholds — they encode one run.

out.description: Where to write the scenario (omit for dry-run)

phaseSignal.description: Scope every check to a phase, e.g. /Robot/State

tools.name: loop_diff
tools.description: Rank how far a run diverged from a known-good baseline log, signal by signal. The largest divergence usually sits closest to the cause; signals present in only one log point at a rename or a subsystem that never initialized.

log.description: Path to the run being investigated

tools.name: mode_a
tools.description: Mode A between-match pass: ingest a log, flag brownout/battery/CAN/loop issues, and persist metrics to the trend store.

db.description: Path to the SQLite trend store

tools.name: mode_a_scan
tools.description: Sweep one or more directories (USB mount point, Driver Station log folder) for .wpilog files not yet in the trend store, and run the Mode A pass on each. Use this to catch up after matches happened without the watcher running; for continuous ingest between matches, run the daemon (`modes watch <db> <dir>...`) instead, which cannot be a tool because it blocks.

db.description: Path to the SQLite trend store

tools.name: swerve_analysis
tools.description: Detect underdamped/oscillating closed-loop behavior from a swerve module signal (hedged PID guidance).

tools.name: vision_analysis
tools.description: Vision detection rate / dropouts from a hasTarget or tag-count signal.

tools.name: loop_timing
tools.description: Loop overrun analysis (vs 20 ms) from a loop-period signal.

tools.name: battery_health
tools.description: Battery droop / internal-resistance indicator with a hedged end-of-match sag projection.

tools.name: anomaly
tools.description: Robust (MAD) outlier detection on one signal.

tools.name: analyze_cycles
tools.description: Scoring cycle-time analysis from a monotonic cycle/score counter: how many cycles, and how fast (mean/median/fastest).

entry.description: Counter signal name (optional; auto-resolved if omitted)

tools.name: signal_stats
tools.description: Summary statistics for one signal (min/max/mean/median/stdDev/p95) with a data-quality block.

tools.name: compare_signals
tools.description: Compare summary statistics of two signals — the same signal across two matches, or two symmetric mechanisms (left vs right).

tools.name: correlate
tools.description: Pearson correlation between two signals (nearest-timestamp aligned). Suggests a relationship; never proves causation.

tools.name: find_peaks
tools.description: Find local maxima in a signal whose prominence exceeds a threshold (current spikes, impact events).

tools.name: rate_of_change
tools.description: Derivative statistics for a signal (units per second) — max/min slope and when the steepest change happened.

tools.name: data_quality
tools.description: Assess how much a signal's sampling actually supports a conclusion (sample count, span, period regularity, confidence).

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the offline documentation index (WPILib, CTRE Phoenix 6, PhotonVision, PathPlanner) with a natural-language question. Use this before answering any API question from memory — the docs are versioned and your recollection of them is not.

query.description: A natural-language question or API name

source.description: Restrict to one corpus: wpilib | ctre | photonvision | pathplanner

tools.name: search_manual
tools.description: Search the indexed game manual PDF for a rule. Returns the passage and its page number so the rule can be verified. Never state a rule from memory — cite the page.

query.description: Rule code (e.g. G410) or a question

tools.name: knowledge_status
tools.description: Show which documentation corpora are indexed and how large each is. Call this if a search returns nothing.

tools.name: nt_status
tools.description: Connect to a live robot's NetworkTables server and report whether the connection is up (live/real-time; read-only).

host.description: Robot NT server host/IP (e.g. 10.TE.AM.2 or localhost)

tools.name: nt_get
tools.description: Read a single live value from NetworkTables by key (read-only; the copilot never writes actuator/enable values).

tools.name: nt_keys
tools.description: List live NetworkTables keys (optionally by prefix).

tools.name: auto_show
tools.description: Summarize a PathPlanner .auto (path references).

tools.name: auto_swap_path
tools.description: Propose swapping a path reference in a .auto. Reviewable diff; writes only if 'out' is given.
